papers.title: Niche-driven divergence of prokaryotic and viral communities in Pogonatum cirratum.
papers.abstract: Ecological niche partitioning shapes microbial communities in terrestrial mosses, yet its underlying mechanisms and associated viral diversity remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil (Rs) and endophytic niche (Pc) of Pogonatum cirratum using amplicon and metagenomic sequencing. Rs exhibited higher species richness, co-dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, whereas Pc was dominated by Pseudomonadota (81.13%) but showed greater functional diversity. Source tracking revealed that 10.57% of Pc taxa origin
papers.summary: This study characterizes prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil and endophytic niche of the moss Pogonatum cirratum, revealing distinct niche-driven community structures with higher species richness in soil but greater functional diversity and dominance of Pseudomonadota in the endosphere. It also identifies a small proportion of endophytic taxa originating from soil and provides insights into associated viral diversity.

papers.title: The Calcidiscus leptoporus genome reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions.
papers.abstract: Coccolithophores are major marine phytoplankton that contribute to ocean carbon cycling through both organic carbon fixation and calcium carbonate biomineralization, yet the functional basis of their interactions with phycosphere bacteria remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a coccolithophore that calcifies in both life-cycle stages. We combined host genome analysis, genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria, and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment to test how B-vitamin biosynthet
papers.summary: This study presents the nuclear genome of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus and combines it with metagenomic and experimental data to reveal that interactions with phycosphere bacteria are mediated by B-vitamin exchange, highlighting a vitamin-based holobiont mechanism. The findings provide new insights into the functional basis of coccolithophore-bacteria symbiosis and its potential role in marine carbon cycling.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Mock Communities as Quality Control Materials for Clinical Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables comprehensive detection of a broad spectrum of microorganisms. However, its clinical application faces two major challenges: the development of appropriate microbiome-based biomarkers and the need to ensure the reproducibility and quality of the microbiome analytical workflow. Therefore, we developed four types of bead-based mock communities as standard materials for microbiome analysis and evaluated potential experimental biases arising from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of four bead-based mock communities designed as quality control materials for clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing. The authors evaluated biases introduced during nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis, providing a standardized resource to improve reproducibility and quality assurance in clinical microbiome workflows.

papers.title: Association between Oral Manifestations and Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease-related Esophageal Diseases: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: This scoping review was conducted to map evidence on associations between oral manifestations and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and its related esophageal diseases, including non-erosive reflux disease, erosive esophagitis, Barrett's esophagus and esophageal adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the existing evidence on how oral manifestations (such as dental erosion and other oral signs) relate to gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and its associated esophageal conditions, including erosive esophagitis and Barrett's esophagus. The findings highlight that oral manifestations are commonly associated with GERD and may serve as useful indicators for early detection of underlying esophageal diseases.

papers.title: ExpoLib: a framework for an MS/MS exposome library of anthropogenic and natural toxicants and their biotransformation products.
papers.abstract: Despite technological advancements over the last three decades in small-molecule omics, compound annotation remains a major bottleneck in untargeted metabolomics and non-targeted environmental analysis. This is especially true for exposomics applications, which remain significantly affected by the limited chemical space coverage.
papers.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
papers.summary: ExpoLib is a new framework for building a comprehensive MS/MS spectral library focused on anthropogenic and natural toxicants and their biotransformation products, addressing the critical bottleneck of compound annotation in exposomics. By expanding chemical space coverage, it aims to improve the identification of environmental exposures in untargeted metabolomics and non-targeted analysis.

papers.title: Deployable high-fidelity metagenome binning at scale with QuickBin.
papers.abstract: Reconstructing genomes from metagenomic assemblies is foundational to microbiome research, yet binning faces a persistent trade-off between fidelity and throughput. Many high-accuracy methods rely on GPU-intensive workflows, marker-gene postprocessing, or heavy computational resources, limiting reproducible use at scale. Here, we present QuickBin, a CPU-native, marker-free binning algorithm designed to recover near-complete, ultra-low-contamination metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) efficiently. QuickBin pairs a GC-coverage spatial index (BinMap) with an early-exit Oracle cascade of similarit
papers.summary: QuickBin is a new CPU-native, marker-free metagenome binning algorithm that recovers near-complete, ultra-low-contamination genomes efficiently without requiring GPU resources. It uses a GC-coverage spatial index and an early-exit Oracle cascade to achieve high-fidelity binning at scale, addressing the trade-off between accuracy and throughput in microbiome research.

papers.title: Community-driven updates for comprehensive long-read metagenomics and enhanced binning in nf-core/mag v5.
papers.abstract: nf-core/mag is a reproducible Nextflow pipeline for best-practice metagenomic de novo assembly, and binning within the nf-core framework. Here we present a major update that adds support for long-read-only assembly and bin refinement, includes five new binning tools, expands taxonomic classification to viruses and eukaryotes, and improves bin quality evaluation with new tools and latest databases. Through sustained community-driven development spanning seven years and four primary curator teams, nf-core/mag remains actively developed as an open-source workflow for metagenomic analysis, benefit
papers.summary: This paper describes a major update to nf-core/mag, a Nextflow pipeline for metagenomic assembly and binning, adding long-read support, five new binning tools, expanded taxonomic classification for viruses and eukaryotes, and improved bin quality evaluation. The update reflects sustained community-driven development over seven years, making it a more comprehensive and up-to-date resource for metagenomics researchers.

papers.title: Desert-derived Ensifer sp. SA403 enhances potato salt tolerance by reshaping rhizosphere microbiome functions and host responses.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization increasingly threatens global food security, and potato (Solanum tuberosum L.), a moderately salt-sensitive crop, is particularly vulnerable to saline soils. Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offer a promising strategy to improve crop performance, yet how PGPR interact with native microorganisms to enhance potato salt tolerance remains poorly understood. In this study, we identified a desert-derived PGPR strain, Ensifer sp. SA403, which substantially enhanced potato performance under high salinity across sterile, non-sterile and field conditions. Physiologically, in
papers.summary: This study identifies a desert-derived plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium, Ensifer sp. SA403, that significantly enhances potato salt tolerance under various conditions, including field trials. The mechanism involves reshaping the rhizosphere microbiome and modulating host physiological responses, offering a promising strategy for sustainable agriculture in saline soils.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified via metagenomic sequencing during a severe disease outbreak in a Serbian kennel. The findings expand the known host range of RFAV and highlight the utility of metagenomic sequencing for diagnosing unusual pathogens in domestic animals.

papers.title: Coenocline Simulation of Microbiome Samples: A Biologically Mechanistic Framework for Generating Ecologically Realistic Synthetic Datasets to Support Classification Method Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Machine learning and statistical classification methods are widely applied to microbiome data for diagnostic, prognostic, and phenotypic insights. However, the complex, multivariate nature of microbiome communities makes it difficult to assess the relative performance of these methods. Most comparisons rely on a small number of published datasets, without considering their underlying ecological properties or how these properties may, in turn, influence classification performance. We introduced a coenocline-based simulation framework to generate synthetic microbiome datasets that incorporate re
papers.summary: This paper introduces a coenocline-based simulation framework for generating synthetic microbiome datasets that mimic real ecological gradients, providing a biologically mechanistic approach to evaluate machine learning classification methods. The framework allows researchers to create ecologically realistic datasets with controlled properties, improving the assessment of classification performance in microbiome studies.

papers.title: Fruits, Vegetables, and Legumes: Harnessing the Gut-Kidney Axis in Hypertensive Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is the most common comorbidity in chronic kidney disease (CKD), affecting roughly 80-85% of patients overall and an even higher proportion in nondialysis CKD G3-G5. This narrative review examines whether, and under what clinical conditions, fruits, vegetables, and legumes can be used safely in adults with hypertensive CKD, especially nondialysis CKD G3-G5, as well as moderate to severe loss of kidney function, paying close attention to the gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, gut-derived uremic toxins, potassium bioavailability, and modifiable clinical risk factors. The clinic
papers.summary: This narrative review evaluates the safety and potential benefits of fruits, vegetables, and legumes in adults with hypertensive chronic kidney disease (CKD), focusing on the gut-kidney axis. It discusses how these foods may modulate gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, and uremic toxins, while considering potassium bioavailability and clinical risk factors for safe dietary recommendations.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein embeddings and genomic context to fill annotation gaps for carbohydrate metabolism genes in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC achieved high cross-validation performance and improved functional coverage, enabling better interpretation of carbohydrate-active enzymes in this ecosystem.

papers.title: The intestinal microbiota mediates inflammatory responses in heat-stressed pigs via the NOD1/RIP2/NF-κB signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: Intestinal inflammation in pigs is widespread, involving complex pathogens, and is exacerbated by heat stress (HS). This study investigated HS alters gut microbiota to activate NOD1/RIP2/NF-κB signaling and induce intestinal inflammation. Twenty pigs exposed to HS (34 ± 1 °C) were compared to 20 controls (25 ± 3 °C). Tissues and feces were collected at intervals. Ninety germ-free mice were randomly divided into nine groups for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments. Histopathological changes in colonic tissue were observed, and inflammatory factors in peripheral blood were quantifi
papers.summary: This study shows that heat stress in pigs alters the gut microbiota, which activates the NOD1/RIP2/NF-κB signaling pathway and triggers intestinal inflammation. Fecal microbiota transplantation experiments in germ-free mice confirmed that the heat-stress-associated microbiota is sufficient to induce inflammatory responses.

papers.title: Deciphering microbial community dynamics using cross-sectional data-informed NeuralODE.
papers.abstract: Understanding the ecological mechanisms of host-associated microbial ecosystems typically relies on either cross-sectional or time-series data. Cross-sectional analyses are limited in their ability to assess intervention effects, whereas time-series models require dense and informative sampling that is often impractical.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a NeuralODE-based framework that leverages cross-sectional data to infer microbial community dynamics, overcoming the limitations of traditional time-series models that require dense sampling. The approach demonstrates that meaningful ecological interactions and intervention effects can be deciphered from static snapshots, offering a practical tool for studying host-associated microbiomes.

papers.title: Computational Genomics for Resistome Characterization: Current Advancements and Future Challenges Under a One Health Perspective.
papers.abstract: The resistome, defined as the complete set of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) present in the microbiota of a given environment, is a critical component for understanding the evolutionary dynamics of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and its impact on human, animal, and environmental health. This review summarizes current methods and technological advances and offers a forward-looking perspective on resistome research. A systematic literature search was conducted. References on short-read and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration were inclu
papers.summary: This review summarizes current computational methods for characterizing the resistome—the collection of antibiotic resistance genes in microbial communities—including short- and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration. It highlights technological advances and future challenges, emphasizing a One Health perspective that links human, animal, and environmental health.

papers.title: Wastewater Metagenomic Reanalysis of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Public Datasets from Türkiye (Ankara and Hatay).
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance in microbial communities is a global health concern that leads to millions of deaths each year. Many bacterial pathogens have resistance to multiple antibiotics. Domestic wastewater treatment facilities are reservoirs for antibiotic-resistant bacteria and resistance genes. Wastewater-based epidemiology surveillance is crucial for monitoring antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Türkiye has one of the highest levels of antibiotic resistance with a lack of research on resistomes. This study is a focused reanalysis of publicly available wastewater met
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed public wastewater metagenomic datasets from Ankara and Hatay in Türkiye to profile antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), addressing a gap in resistome surveillance for a country with high antibiotic resistance. The findings highlight wastewater treatment facilities as key reservoirs of ARGs and demonstrate the utility of reusing public metagenomic data for epidemiological monitoring.

papers.title: Konjac Glucomannan: From Molecular Architecture to Translational Applications-A Critical Review of Structure-Function Relationships, Emerging Biomedical Frontiers, and Industrial Challenges.
papers.abstract: Konjac glucomannan (KGM) is a plant-derived polysaccharide with a long history of food use and a rapidly expanding portfolio of biomedical applications. Yet despite decades of research, translation of KGM-based materials from laboratory proof-of-concept to clinical and commercial products remains slow, hampered by unresolved structural controversies, batch-to-batch variability, and a lack of quantitative design rules. This review provides a critical, mechanism-focused analysis of KGM across its molecular architecture, extraction and modification, and translational applications, moving beyond c
papers.summary: This review critically examines konjac glucomannan (KGM), a plant polysaccharide with established food use and emerging biomedical applications, focusing on the gap between laboratory research and clinical/commercial translation. It highlights unresolved structural controversies, batch variability, and the lack of quantitative design rules as key barriers, and calls for mechanism-focused approaches to bridge molecular architecture and practical applications.

papers.title: How Gut Microbiota Influence Healthy Aging: Overview of Reviews.
papers.abstract: Background: Gut microbiota plays a key role in the aging process, with age-related microbial shifts contributing to chronic inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, frailty, and cognitive decline. Despite growing interest, an integrated synthesis of how diet and lifestyle modifications influence gut microbiota remains limited. This overview of reviews summarizes the current evidence on how dietary and lifestyle interventions shape microbial composition and affect aging outcomes. Methods: Following the PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed and Scopus for English-language reviews (January 2023-Octob
papers.summary: This overview of reviews synthesizes current evidence on how dietary and lifestyle interventions shape gut microbiota composition and influence aging outcomes, highlighting the role of microbial shifts in chronic inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, frailty, and cognitive decline. The authors note that while interest is growing, integrated syntheses remain limited, and they call for more comprehensive approaches to understand how modifiable factors can promote healthy aging.

papers.title: Land-Use and Depth-Dependent Assembly of Soil Microbiomes Shapes Ecological Functions, Interaction Networks, and Phytopathogenic Communities Across Crop and Orchard Systems.
papers.abstract: Soil microorganisms are essential for nutrient cycling, plant productivity, and soil health, yet the relative importance of land-use and soil depth in shaping agricultural microbiomes remains poorly understood. This study investigated soil microbial communities across uncultivated land, alfalfa fields, crop systems (feed corn and sweet corn), and orchard systems (walnut and quince) in the Hajdúnánás region of Hungary using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and soil physicochemical analyses. Microbial alpha diversity showed limited variation among land-use systems but declined significantly with s
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to examine how land-use type and soil depth shape microbial communities in agricultural soils, finding that depth had a stronger effect on diversity than land use. The authors linked these microbial shifts to changes in ecological functions, interaction networks, and the abundance of phytopathogenic communities, providing insights for managing soil health in crop and orchard systems.

papers.title: Tumor Location and Preoperative Biliary Stenting Shape Gut Microbiome Diversity in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Recent evidence suggests that gut microbiome plays a role in the development of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and influences treatment response. However, the association of tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) with gut microbial composition and diversity remains poorly understood. Methods: Preoperative stool specimens were prospectively collected from patients with PDAC undergoing surgery between March 2020 and July 2021 at the Department of Surgery, Heidelberg University Hospital, Germany. Whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed. Micro
papers.summary: This study investigates how tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) affect the gut microbiome in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients. Using whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing of preoperative stool samples, the authors found that both tumor location and PBS significantly shape gut microbial diversity and composition, suggesting these clinical factors should be considered in microbiome-based studies and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Precision Nutrigenomics in Cultured Finfish: Dietary Regulation of Gene Expression, Microbial Ecology, Metabolism, and Immunity.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrigenomics requires a diet-microbiome-host perspective because microorganisms can transform feed substrates, generate bioactive metabolites, compete with pathogens, and modify intestinal and systemic gene regulation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative controlled feeding trials, transcriptomic and targeted gene-expression studies, microbiome analyses, and complementary multi-omic evidence concerning dietary regulations in cultured finfish. The available evidence is concentrated particularly on soybean-derived proteins, lipid-source replacements, selected am
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from controlled feeding trials and multi-omic studies to show how diet composition, particularly soybean-derived proteins and lipid replacements, regulates gene expression, gut microbial ecology, metabolism, and immunity in cultured finfish. It emphasizes the need for a diet-microbiome-host perspective in precision nutrigenomics for aquaculture.

papers.title: Comparison of Inoculation Routes for Honeybee Gut Microbiota Assembly Under Laboratory Conditions.
papers.abstract: The honeybee (Apis mellifera) gut microbiota serves as a model for host-microbe studies, as newly emerged workers provide a low-complexity, nearly germ-free system. Although multiple inoculation strategies are commonly applied under laboratory conditions, their comparative effects on microbial colonization remain incompletely understood. Here, we systematically compared four commonly used inoculation strategies, including pollen mixture feeding, oral feeding, dunk inoculation, and comb-exposed inoculation, under controlled laboratory conditions using an identical microbial source. We assessed
papers.summary: This study systematically compares four common methods for inoculating honeybee gut microbiota under laboratory conditions, finding that the inoculation route significantly affects microbial colonization patterns. The results provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate inoculation strategies in host-microbe research using honeybees.

papers.title: Microbial Functional Potentials Differ Among Monospecific and Mixed Moss Biocrusts in an Alpine Sandy Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Moss-dominated biological soil crusts are associated with carbon and nitrogen cycling in dryland and alpine sandy ecosystems, but functional differentiation among closely related moss species and their mixed assemblages remains unclear. We used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare below-crust soil associated with Didymodon constrictus (Mitt.) K. Saito (D. constrictus) crusts (mossC), ferrugineus (Schimp. ex Besch.) M.O. Hill (D. ferrugineus) crusts (mossF), and visually co-dominated mixed crusts (mossM) in the Gonghe Basin on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Fifteen spatially separ
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the functional potential of soil microbial communities beneath monospecific and mixed moss biocrusts in an alpine sandy ecosystem, finding that microbial functional profiles differ among crust types. The results suggest that moss species identity and assemblage composition shape below-crust microbial functions, with implications for carbon and nitrogen cycling in these ecosystems.

papers.title: Oral Cavity Antibacterial Discovery Pipeline Driven by Advanced Analytical Techniques.
papers.abstract: The oral cavity represents an extremely complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem capable of rapidly adapting to antimicrobial stress. These characteristics make it a promising environment for the identification of novel bioactive molecules with therapeutic potential. At the same time, the increasing prevalence of resistant pathogens in dental and oral-maxillofacial infections highlights the limitations of current therapeutic strategies and the urgent need for new effective antibacterial agents. This review examines the central role of advanced analytical techniques, with particular emphasis on
papers.summary: This review discusses the oral cavity as a rich source for discovering novel antibacterial compounds, highlighting the urgent need for new agents due to rising antimicrobial resistance. It emphasizes the role of advanced analytical techniques in identifying and characterizing these bioactive molecules from the complex oral microbiome.

papers.title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to Childhood Obesity: T2DM and MASLD Risk Predictive Models.
papers.abstract: Pediatric obesity is a complex, multifactorial pandemic with serious early-onset comorbidities, including prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and cardiovascular disorders. While lifestyle modifications and the Mediterranean diet remain primary interventions, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a critical tool for early diagnosis and personalized management. This review evaluates the current role of AI in predicting and treating childhood obesity and its complications. A literature search was conducted on PubMed and Google Scho
papers.summary: This review evaluates the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predicting and managing childhood obesity and its complications, such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. It highlights AI as an emerging tool for early diagnosis and personalized treatment, complementing traditional lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: The Dietary Inclusion of Corn and Peas Affects the Fecal Bacterial Diversity and Composition of Sarda Goats.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary inclusion of corn and peas on the fecal microbiota composition and functional potential in Sarda goats. Twelve female goats were allocated to two groups, a group grazing on a natural pasture (GP) and a group grazing on the same pasture with a diet enriched with corn and peas (GC), both grain supplements at 100 g/day. Fecal samples were collected, freeze-dried and subjected to 16S rRNA gene sequencing of the V4-V5 region, followed by bioinformatic and statistical analyses. Alpha diversity metrics indicated a significant reduction in microbial richn
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study examined how supplementing the diet of Sarda goats with corn and peas affects their fecal bacterial diversity and composition. The researchers found that the dietary supplementation significantly reduced microbial richness and altered the fecal microbiota, indicating that grain supplements can impact gut microbial communities in goats.

papers.title: Sodium Butyrate Therapy in Ulcerative Colitis: A Systematic Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sodium butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid produced by gut microbial fermentation of dietary fiber, has attracted increasing interest as a potential adjunctive therapy for ulcerative colitis (UC) because of its anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective, and immunomodulatory properties. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the current clinical and preclinical evidence regarding the efficacy and mechanisms of sodium butyrate in UC. Methods: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437741). PubMed/ME
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluates the evidence for sodium butyrate as a therapy for ulcerative colitis, summarizing its anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective, and immunomodulatory effects from preclinical and clinical studies. The findings support its potential as an adjunctive treatment, though the authors highlight the need for more robust clinical trials to confirm efficacy and establish dosing guidelines.

papers.title: Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov., a Fly-Associated Bacterium with Human Gut Metagenomic Representatives: Genomic and Metagenomic Insights into Its Ecological Distribution.
papers.abstract: The genus Vagococcus comprises Gram-positive bacteria with a broad ecological distribution, yet its diversity and potential links between animal and human habitats remain underexplored. Here, we report two novel fly-associated strains, CY52-2T and CY62-2, isolated from a retail market in Beijing, China. Polyphasic taxonomic analyses demonstrated that they represent a novel species, for which we propose the name Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov. Large-scale mining of 805 public metagenomes identified two human gut-derived genomes that share > 99.3% ANI with V. changpingensis, extending the kno
papers.summary: This study describes a new bacterial species, Vagococcus changpingensis, isolated from flies in a Beijing market, and uses genomic and metagenomic analyses to show that closely related genomes are also present in human gut metagenomes, suggesting potential animal-human ecological links. The findings expand the known diversity of the Vagococcus genus and highlight the utility of metagenomic mining for uncovering environmental distribution.

papers.title: KEGG-Based Functional Signatures Complement Taxonomic Profiles Associated with Spontaneous Decolonisation of Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales.
papers.abstract: Understanding the functional potential of the gut microbiota for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) decolonisation is essential for developing novel non-antibiotic strategies to promote their clearance. In a previous study, we identified distinct taxonomic signatures associated with spontaneous CRE decolonisation (DeCol). Here, we aimed to determine whether these taxonomic differences were accompanied by differences in the predicted functional potential of the gut microbiota. Patients were identified from a database of individuals colonised with CRE. We performed Illumina shotgun meta
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the gut microbiota's functional potential, predicted via KEGG pathways from shotgun metagenomic data, differs between patients who spontaneously clear carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and those who remain colonized. The authors find that functional signatures complement previously identified taxonomic differences, offering insights into microbial mechanisms that may promote CRE decolonization and informing non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Bat-Associated Parvoviruses: High Genetic Diversity and Novel Viruses in Gia Lai and Dong Nai Provinces, Vietnam.
papers.abstract: Bats are recognized as key reservoirs for diverse viruses, including members of the Parvoviridae family. Vietnam hosts an exceptionally wide variety of bat species, yet the diversity of parvoviruses in these populations remains largely unexplored. This study provides the first survey of parvoviruses in bats from Gia Lai and Dong Nai provinces, screening 150 samples from 26 bat species and detecting parvoviruses in 38 (25%). A total of 45 viral operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were identified, encompassing four parvoviral subfamilies: Parvovirinae, Densovirinae, Penbrevirinae, and Hamavirinae
papers.summary: This study presents the first survey of parvoviruses in bats from two provinces in Vietnam, screening 150 samples from 26 bat species and detecting parvoviruses in 25% of samples. They identified 45 viral operational taxonomic units spanning four parvoviral subfamilies, revealing high genetic diversity and novel viruses in these bat populations.

papers.title: Pooled Shotgun Metagenomics Reveals Cloacal Microbiota Composition and Resistome Patterns in Chickens from Kazakhstan.
papers.abstract: Monitoring poultry microbiota and antimicrobial resistance genes is important, as they can reflect flock health, farm conditions, and the level of antimicrobial resistance. Although shotgun metagenomics has been widely applied worldwide to investigate poultry microbiota and antimicrobial resistance, comparable baseline datasets describing the cloacal microbiota and resistome of poultry in Kazakhstan are scarce. In this study, taxonomic and resistome profiles were characterized in pooled metagenomes of the cloacal microbiota of chickens sampled from household and industrial poultry farms in Kaz
papers.summary: This study provides the first baseline dataset of cloacal microbiota and antimicrobial resistance genes in chickens from Kazakhstan using pooled shotgun metagenomics, revealing differences between household and industrial farm settings. The findings highlight the utility of metagenomic surveillance for monitoring poultry health and antimicrobial resistance in understudied regions.

papers.title: Emergent function, not microbial conformity: functional redundancy and the limits of taxonomic inference in microbiome genomics.
papers.abstract: Microbiome genomics has achieved remarkable resolution of community structure, yet composition alone remains an unstable basis for inferring host-relevant biology. That instability reflects a broader interpretive problem in which taxonomically distinct communities can converge on similar outputs, while superficially similar communities can diverge in behaviour because of strain variation, gene content, regulatory state, ecological context, spatial organization and host physiology. Functional redundancy is therefore better understood not as a reserve of interchangeable organisms but as a distri
papers.summary: This perspective argues that taxonomic composition is an unreliable proxy for microbiome function because functionally redundant communities can be taxonomically distinct, while similar communities can behave differently due to strain-level variation, gene content, and ecological context. It reframes functional redundancy as a distributed property rather than a pool of interchangeable organisms, emphasizing the need for function-focused approaches in microbiome genomics.

papers.title: theBIGbam: compression and interactive exploration of large-scale sequencing alignments with circular mapping support.
papers.abstract: theBIGbam (github.com/bhagavadgitadu22/theBIGbam) is a genome browser and alignment viewer designed for massive metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets. The tool takes BAM files containing read alignments, together with genome assemblies in FASTA format or annotated genome sequences in GenBank format. Alternatively, it can start from raw FASTQ reads and generate alignments using a modified mapper that supports circular genomes, enabling seamless read mapping across genome ends. theBIGbam can compress hundreds of gigabytes of input files 10- to 100-fold into dedicated databases while retain
papers.summary: theBIGbam is a new genome browser and alignment viewer that efficiently compresses large metagenomic and metatranscriptomic BAM files (10- to 100-fold) and supports interactive exploration of alignments, including circular genome mapping. It can also process raw FASTQ reads with a modified mapper that handles circular genomes, making it useful for microbial genomics.

papers.title: ViralQC: a tool for assessing completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs.
papers.abstract: Viruses represent the most abundant biological entities on Earth, playing vital roles in diverse ecosystems. Cataloging viruses across various environments is essential for understanding their properties and functions. Metagenomic sequencing has emerged as the most comprehensive method for virus discovery. However, distinguishing viral sequences from the vast background of microbial organisms in metagenomic data remains a significant challenge. Existing tools experience varying degrees of false positive rates due to noise in sequencing and assembly, and the integration of proviruses into micro
papers.summary: ViralQC is a new tool that assesses the completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs from metagenomic data, addressing the challenge of false positives in virus discovery. It helps researchers distinguish genuine viral sequences from noise and microbial contamination, improving the reliability of viral cataloging.

papers.title: Immune Cell-Mediated Causal Link Between Gut Microbiota Traits and Childhood Asthma: Evidence From Mendelian Randomization and Metagenomic Sequencing.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota may be involved in childhood asthma. However, the causal relationship between the gut microbiota and childhood asthma remains obscure. Whether immune cells mediate the pathway from gut microbiota to childhood asthma has not been elucidated.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and metagenomic sequencing to investigate the causal relationship between gut microbiota traits and childhood asthma, finding evidence that specific microbial features influence asthma risk. It also suggests that immune cells may mediate this pathway, providing new insights into the gut-lung axis in pediatric asthma.

papers.title: Microbiome and aging: Trajectories of microbiome age across human ecosystems and their systemic effects.
papers.abstract: The "microbiome age," a computationally derived systemic biosignature, is emerging as a pivotal framework for deciphering host aging trajectories and multi-organ health status. Beyond merely cataloging taxonomic shifts within specific niches, this concept integrates the cumulative biological effects of microbial community structure, functional homeostasis, ecological interactions, and host regulatory dynamics over time. Accumulating evidence indicates that a deviation between chronological and microbiome age-termed the "microbiome age gap"-closely correlates with systemic declines in immunomod
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging concept of 'microbiome age' as a systemic biosignature that reflects host aging trajectories and multi-organ health. It highlights that the 'microbiome age gap'—the deviation between chronological and microbiome age—correlates with systemic declines in immunomodulation and other age-related processes, suggesting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Wekemo Bioincloud 2026: An AI-enabled platform for standardized multi-omics data analyses.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of multi-omics data has created an increasing demand for accessible and reproducible platforms for integrative analysis. Here, we present Wekemo Bioincloud 2026, a comprehensive upgrade of the original platform, providing 41 standardized workflows (expanded from 22) across nine analytical categories, including a newly introduced correlation analysis module for cross-omics association studies. Visualization capabilities have been substantially expanded to 126 tools (from 65), incorporating artificial intelligence (AI)-guided parameter selection and automated image interpreta
papers.summary: Wekemo Bioincloud 2026 is an upgraded cloud platform that now offers 41 standardized multi-omics analysis workflows and 126 visualization tools, including a new correlation analysis module for cross-omics studies. It integrates AI-guided parameter selection and automated image interpretation to make complex analyses more accessible and reproducible.

papers.title: Microbial Variability in Zoo-Housed Alaotran Gentle Lemurs: Host-Associated Factors and Environmental Influences.
papers.abstract: Primates worldwide face escalating ecological pressures, driving many species to rapid declines. Modern zoos play an essential role by maintaining viable populations and improving welfare through research-driven management. However, gut-microbiome interactions in captive primates remain poorly understood. Our study investigated how host-specific traits influence fecal microbiota composition, whether shared environments facilitate shared microbial signatures, and whether fluctuations in fecal cortisol and testosterone correspond to microbial changes. We also evaluated the combined use of hormon
papers.summary: This study examines how host-specific traits, shared environments, and hormone fluctuations influence the fecal microbiota of zoo-housed Alaotran gentle lemurs. The findings reveal that host factors and environmental conditions shape microbial composition, with cortisol and testosterone levels correlating with microbial changes, providing insights for improving captive primate welfare.

papers.title: The Gut Mycobiome in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Reframing Candida as a Signal of Ecosystem Disruption.
papers.abstract: Growing interest in the gut mycobiome has renewed focus on Candida spp. in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Yet, fecal detection remains difficult to interpret, given its uncertain relationship with intestinal inflammation. This narrative review synthesizes historical, mechanistic, observational, and interventional evidence to distinguish colonization, relative abundance, mucosal invasion, virulence transitions, and potential contributions to IBD.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the gut mycobiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), focusing on the role of Candida species. It argues that fecal detection of Candida should be interpreted as a signal of ecosystem disruption rather than a direct cause of inflammation, and distinguishes between colonization, relative abundance, mucosal invasion, and virulence transitions.

papers.title: Bioactive Components and Functional Applications of Sea Buckthorn: A Review.
papers.abstract: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) is a medicinal and edible plant rich in polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids, carotenoids, and polysaccharides. These constituents are associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, gut microbiota-modulating, antibacterial, and other health-related activities, supporting its potential use in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics. However, its composition and bioactivity vary with plant part, extract type, and processing method, which complicates comparison across studies. This review evaluates sea buckthorn as
papers.summary: This review consolidates current knowledge on sea buckthorn's bioactive components, including polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids, and polysaccharides, and their associated health benefits such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and gut microbiota-modulating activities. It highlights the variability in composition and bioactivity due to plant part, extract type, and processing, which complicates cross-study comparisons, and discusses its potential applications in functional foods, nutraceuticals, and cosmetics.

papers.title: The multi-omics fallacy in microbiome science.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine-learning-assisted multi-omics have expanded the scale and ambition of microbiome research, but they have also sharpened an older interpretive problem. Biologically plausible structure is too easily mistaken for biological explanation. This Perspective defines the multi-omics fallacy as claim inflation that occurs when integrating microbial, host, environmental, spatial, and clinical data is assumed to move interpretation from association toward verified mechanism without a corresponding gain in measurement, localization, temporal resolution, functional linka
papers.summary: This Perspective paper defines the 'multi-omics fallacy' in microbiome research, where integrating diverse data types (microbial, host, environmental, etc.) is mistakenly assumed to automatically yield mechanistic insight. The authors argue that biologically plausible structure is often over-interpreted as biological explanation, and that true mechanism requires additional validation beyond mere data integration.

papers.title: Ecological assembly of mucosal and fecal microbiomes in ulcerative colitis across genes, functions, and species.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with gut microbial dysbiosis, yet the ecological processes underlying community assembly remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how gut microbial communities assemble in ulcerative colitis patients by analyzing mucosal and fecal microbiomes across genes, functions, and species. It reveals that ecological assembly processes differ between these niches and are disrupted in disease, providing insights into the dysbiosis associated with IBD.

papers.title: Multi-layer gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes despite preserved higher-order community structure.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) has been consistently associated with alterations in the gut microbiome, although disease, treatment, diet, and other host factors may contribute to the observed patterns. How these associations are organized across different biological levels of the microbial ecosystem remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study examines gut microbiome variation in type 2 diabetes across multiple biological levels, finding that while specific taxa and functional pathways differ between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals, the higher-order community structure (e.g., co-occurrence networks) remains largely preserved. The results suggest that T2D-associated microbiome changes are localized to lower-level features rather than global community organization.

papers.title: Using nanopore metagenomics to characterize pathogens in febrile patients from a highland of Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: Febrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa despite substantial reductions in malaria transmission. As malaria positive cases decrease, an increasing number of patients with febrile illnesses test negative for Plasmodium infection, leaving their causes unresolved. As a result of the diagnostic gap, patients receive presumptive antimalarial treatment, unnecessary antibiotics and experience delayed therapy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomics to identify potential pathogens in febrile patients from a highland region of Western Kenya, aiming to address the diagnostic gap for non-malarial febrile illnesses. The approach demonstrates the utility of metagenomic sequencing for pathogen detection in clinical samples, potentially improving diagnosis and treatment in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses the use of agentic AI to generate trustworthy synthetic microbial genomic data, emphasizing the need for biological plausibility and computational validation. It highlights the potential of genomic foundation models for genome-level generation and design, while calling for robust governance frameworks to ensure reliability and reproducibility.

papers.title: Genome-resolved insights into hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microbial communities from deep petroleum reservoir cores of the Nashpa Oil Field, Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities from deep subsurface petroleum reservoirs are adapted to hydrocarbon-rich, oxygen-limited, and physicochemically extreme environments. However, genome-resolved knowledge of petroleum reservoir microbiomes from Pakistan remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study provides the first genome-resolved analysis of microbial communities in deep petroleum reservoir cores from Pakistan's Nashpa Oil Field, revealing diverse hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microorganisms. The findings expand our understanding of subsurface microbial life in extreme, hydrocarbon-rich environments and highlight potential biogeochemical roles in petroleum reservoirs.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into microbial communities of terrestrial mud volcanos: functional diversity of subsurface archaea and bacteria.
papers.abstract: Terrestrial mud volcanoes are surface geological features where fluidized sediments and gasses from the subsurface are discharged along a fracture network providing a window into the deep biosphere. Although mud volcanoes constitute an important source of methane emission from natural environments, their microbial communities responsible for methane cycling remain poorly characterized. Using a metagenomics approach, we investigated the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of microbial communities in three active mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman mud volcanic province. Despite the volca
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize the microbial communities in three terrestrial mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman province, revealing the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of subsurface archaea and bacteria, with a focus on methane cycling. The findings provide new insights into the functional diversity of deep biosphere microorganisms and their role in natural methane emissions.

papers.title: Wastewater treatment plant effluent alters particle-associated bacterial assemblages in an intermittent stream.
papers.abstract: Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) can be point-sources of nutrients, organic matter, anthropogenic contaminants, and microbes to lotic environments, and the input of WWTP effluent can alter the activity and composition of stream microbial assemblages in the benthos and water column. Within the stream benthos, fine particulate matter (FPM) supports especially high levels of microbial activity, but the effect of WWTP effluents on the microbial communities specifically associated with benthic FPM in rivers has not been studied. The present work sought to address this knowledge gap by analyzing
papers.summary: This study investigates how wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluent affects microbial communities attached to fine particulate matter (FPM) in the benthos of an intermittent stream. The findings reveal that effluent input significantly alters the composition of particle-associated bacterial assemblages, highlighting a previously understudied impact of WWTP discharge on stream ecosystems.

papers.title: PUDU (pipeline for universal diversity unveiling): an accessible end-to-end workflow for taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization of environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing.
papers.abstract: Environmental microbiome research has advanced through three complementary sequencing modalities, targeted 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, whole-genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomics, and long-read full-length 16S rRNA profiling, each supported by distinct toolsets with heterogeneous outputs, variable configurations, and different levels of reproducibility documentation. Existing pipelines are typically modality-specific, require substantial configuration expertise, or produce outputs that need further custom scripting before standard ecological analyses can begin. This analytical fragmentation intr
papers.summary: PUDU is a new end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline that unifies taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization for environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing data. It aims to reduce the need for extensive configuration and custom scripting by providing a reproducible, accessible workflow that handles all three modalities.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterization of Nitrite-Negative Urinary Tract Infections and Identification of an optrA-fexA Co-Localization in a Primary Healthcare Setting in China.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) showing negative nitrite results create a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. The plasmid-mediated resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and tet(X) (tigecycline) pose severe therapeutic challenges, but their genomic context in primary healthcare settings remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize nitrite-negative urinary tract infections (UTIs) in a primary healthcare setting in China, revealing the presence of Gram-positive pathogens that are often missed by standard diagnostics. The authors identify a plasmid co-localizing the antibiotic resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and fexA (chloramphenicol/florfenicol), highlighting a potential reservoir of multidrug resistance in community-acquired UTIs.

papers.title: Cross sectional analysis of gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study investigated the differences in gut microbiota in patients with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), exploring their cross-sectional associations with nutritional intake.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared the gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), finding differences in microbial composition that were associated with nutritional intake. The results suggest that PEG feeding may influence the gut microbiome in ALS patients, potentially relevant for disease management.

papers.title: Gut microbiome and functional adaptations to paleo and rational diets in professional athletes: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Nutrient-rich dietary patterns are recognized as important modulators of gut microbiota diversity, whereas restrictive diets may increase the risk of microbial depletion and functional imbalance. Among alternative nutritional strategies, the Paleo diet has been considered for its potential applicability in sports nutrition, however, evidence regarding its effects on the gut microbiome remains limited. This study aimed to analyze and compare the taxonomic structure and functional potential of the gut microbiome in professional handball players following an 8-week isocaloric Paleo or rational di
papers.summary: This pilot study compared the gut microbiome of professional handball players following an 8-week isocaloric Paleo diet versus a rational diet, finding that the Paleo diet was associated with distinct taxonomic and functional changes in the gut microbiome. The results suggest that while both diets are feasible in athletic populations, the Paleo diet may alter microbial composition and functional potential in ways that could impact athlete health and performance, though further research is needed.

papers.title: HPV vaccination associates with Lactobacillus crispatus-dominant vaginal microbiota in women with cervical lesions: a metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination provides high-level protection against cervical cancer through type-specific antibodies, although breakthrough and persistent high-risk HPV (hrHPV) infections may still occur in some vaccinated women. In addition to neutralizing antibodies, vaccination elicits other immune mechanisms that may influence viral persistence and disease progression. Because mucosal immunity is closely linked to the vaginal microbiota, microbial composition may also play an important role in HPV susceptibility, with Lactobacillus crispatus dominance associated with protection,
papers.summary: This metagenomic study found that women with cervical lesions who had received the HPV vaccine were more likely to have a vaginal microbiota dominated by Lactobacillus crispatus, a species associated with protection against HPV. The findings suggest that HPV vaccination may influence the vaginal microbiome, potentially contributing to its protective effects beyond antibody-mediated immunity.

papers.title: A generalized supervised contrastive learning framework for integrative multi-omics prediction models.
papers.abstract: Advancements in multi-omics research have demonstrated the potential of integrating human microbiome and metabolomics data to better understand physiological processes and improve prediction accuracy in studies of human health. While conventional models utilizing single-omics data provide valuable perspectives, they often fail to capture the complexity of biological systems. Recent developments in supervised contrastive learning frameworks have enhanced predictive performance for categorical responses, yet limitations persist in extending these methods to continuous outcomes. A robust model ca
papers.summary: This paper introduces a generalized supervised contrastive learning framework that extends multi-omics integration to continuous outcomes, addressing a key limitation of existing methods that only handle categorical responses. The framework improves prediction accuracy by integrating human microbiome and metabolomics data, offering a more robust approach for modeling complex biological systems in health studies.

papers.title: Oral microbiome classification of elevated salivary glucose in a large adolescent Kuwaiti population.
papers.abstract: The oral cavity harbors a complex microbial ecosystem that reflects both local and systemic health. Metabolic disorders, including impaired glucose regulation, are known to alter the oral microbiome; however, whether oral microbial signatures can classify elevated salivary glucose status in large, healthy pediatric populations has received limited investigation.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether oral microbiome signatures can classify elevated salivary glucose levels in a large cohort of healthy adolescents from Kuwait. The findings suggest that specific microbial profiles are associated with higher salivary glucose, indicating the potential of oral microbiome analysis as a non-invasive screening tool for early metabolic risk.

papers.title: Oral dysbiosis: methodological evolution, the mobile resistome and the future of machine learning in dentistry.
papers.abstract: The oral microbiome acts as a significant, yet often overlooked, reservoir for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). This review examines the role of the human resistome in oral health, evaluating current knowledge on the composition, function and dissemination of ARGs within the oral cavity. By comparing conventional culture-based methodologies against recent whole-genome sequencing (WGS) studies, we assess the critical role of the oral‒gut axis in resistance dissemination. The current literature indicates that horizontal gene transfer (HGT) facilitates the spread of mobile genetic elements
papers.summary: This review highlights the oral microbiome as a significant reservoir for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and examines the role of the oral resistome in health and disease. It compares traditional culture-based methods with whole-genome sequencing approaches, emphasizing the oral-gut axis and horizontal gene transfer in the dissemination of resistance. The paper also discusses the potential of machine learning in advancing dental diagnostics and resistance prediction.

papers.title: Application-focused validation of a viability-selective PMA-qPCR assay for selected skin-associated and cosmetic-relevant bacteria.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of viable bacteria is essential for ensuring product safety and quality in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetics industries. However, conventional plate culture methods are time-consuming and fail to detect viable but non-culturable (VBNC) cells, which frequently occur under environmental stress or preservation conditions and can influence product stability and safety. Accordingly, the need for a quantification method that accounts for VBNC cells has increased. In this study, we optimized and validated a viability-selective quantification method by combining propidium
papers.summary: This study optimized and validated a PMA-qPCR method for selectively quantifying viable bacteria relevant to skin and cosmetics, addressing the limitation of plate counting which misses viable but non-culturable (VBNC) cells. The method provides a faster and more accurate alternative for quality control in the cosmetics industry.
